teaching.hint: Which courses can be taken immediately, and what information changes after one of them is completed?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Finishing all courses is possible exactly when the prerequisite graph contains no directed cycle.
solution_outline.approach: Direct every edge from a prerequisite to its dependent course. Repeatedly remove a course with no remaining prerequisites and decrement the counts of its dependents; succeed only if every course is removed.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: A course's remaining prerequisite count equals its incoming edges from courses not yet removed, so zero-count courses are currently legal to take.
solution_outline.correctness: Removing a zero-count course is valid and faithfully exposes newly available dependents. If removal stops early, each remaining vertex has an incoming edge, which in a finite graph implies a cycle. Conversely, an acyclic directed graph always has a zero-indegree vertex, so all courses are removed exactly when completion is possible.
solution_outline.complexity: Building and processing the graph costs O(V + E) time and O(V + E) space.
solution_outline.pitfall: Reversing the prerequisite edge direction makes indegree mean the wrong condition and can accept or reject the wrong instances.

accepted_alternatives: Depth-first traversal with visiting and completed states, rejecting a back edge to a currently visiting course.
common_wrong_turns: Checking only whether every course appears in some pair
Declaring a graph with no prerequisite pairs impossible
source_fidelity_notes: Examples were omitted; pair direction, label range, unique-pair guarantee, and course and edge bounds were retained.
